snapshotBenchmark.fixture: Git worktree with 20000 files under ignored node_modules; tracked and unignored source retained
snapshotBenchmark.operation: snapshotIdentity, excluding fixture creation and cleanup
snapshotBenchmark.samples: individual standalone executions, not a statistical distribution

executedRegressions: Ignored dependencies and internal junctions do not change identity
Tracked content, tracked deletions and nonignored untracked files do change identity
Non-Git link target strings hash without following external or cyclic targets
Same-size rewrites with restored modification time do not reuse stale cached hashes
Executed checks can write ignored caches without staling their observation
Initialized submodule content changes invalidate parent identity
Native Windows birth lookup succeeds with empty PATH; forced CIM fallback matches normalized identity
Transient unknown birth lookup retries on later acquisition
Live local lock release permits bounded retry; stale, remote and malformed locks require existing explicit recovery
Remaining private account/rejected-PR note removed from current changelog
limits: Existing runs require a new checkpoint and recollected evidence after the inventory scope change.
Ignored untracked inputs and external symlink target content are outside snapshot identity; track relevant inputs.
Metadata caching assumes trustworthy filesystem metadata and does not defeat same-user tampering.
The benchmark covers one Windows fixture; large tracked trees and other hosts were not benchmarked.
Snapshot streaming is bounded per snapshot; separate processes and simultaneous calls are separate workers.
Blocked PowerShell/CIM or inaccessible Windows PID data can still yield unknown birth and remain protected.
Process lookup can add up to three seconds beyond the 1500 ms lock polling budget.
Native Stop timeout behavior and native false-completion blocking remain unverified.
Prior Git history and already shared copies were not rewritten.
